Subject: NorthStar: Capacity bridge & post-incident confirmation

Hi Asha / Tom —

Thanks again for your patience this morning. Brief summary for NorthStar ops: between 08:12–08:48 UTC we saw sustained queueing on your Dedicated GPU pool serving model ns-gpt-large caused by an autoscaler control-plane race that prevented new nodes from being provisioned. That led to request queuing and elevated latency for ~36 minutes.

What we did immediately:
- Opened a control-plane hotfix to stop the race (mitigated at 08:50 UTC).
- Manually bridged capacity with two warm reserved nodes to drain backlog.
- Rolled a configuration to enforce a conservative warmup window for your pool.

Current status: traffic is fully routed and latency is back to expected levels; we continue to monitor. Attached is a diagnostic bundle with logs and metrics from the period: diagnostic_bundle_1129.tar.gz.

Next steps I propose:
1) We will share a draft RCA and a proposed remediation timeline by tomorrow morning (Ben is drafting the RCA).
2) We will propose a one-time credit to cover elevated tail latency and failed requests during the window.
3) Follow-up review call with your SREs and our platform team (30–45m) — please propose slots.

Ask for you: please confirm whether the attached bundle is sufficient for your compliance/audit needs or if you need additional evidence (e.g., raw metrics or specific traces).

Sorry for the disruption — we understand this is impacting NorthStar production traffic. We have treated this as a high priority and will provide the full postmortem and action items ASAP.

Thanks,

Camila / NorthStar team —

Sharing a short technical summary and the draft RCA attached (rca-draft-northstar-1129.pdf). Key points:

Root cause (short): a scheduler race in the Dedicated autoscaler where two concurrent allocation reconciliations could both evaluate pool capacity as below threshold and attempt to provision the same warm slots. The race left the pool stuck in a transient state where the allocator thought provisioning was inflight while the control-plane rate limiter dropped subsequent provisioning requests.

Contributing factors:
- A regression in the allocator backoff introduced in v2.14.1 that reduced the window for re-evaluating inflight provisioning requests.
- NorthStar’s steady-state QPS pattern included short bursts that lined up with the race window.

Immediate fixes applied:
- Reverted the allocator backoff change (hotfix released 08:50 UTC).
- Added a short-lived operator guard to force-provision when backlog > 80% for this pool.
- Increased observability on allocation hang signals and added an alert on inflight-provision-time > 10s.

Planned remediation:
- Permanent allocator fix in v2.14.2 (scheduled rollout 2028-12-05).
- Backfill test harness to simulate bursty QPS against our warmup logic (target 2028-12-12).
- Post-release canary for NorthStar pool for 72h with rollback thresholds.

Attachment: rca-draft-northstar-1129.pdf (contains timeline, hashes for logs, and command logs).

Ben Carter
Principal Services Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Monitoring / safeguards

- If you need additional artifacts (HMAC-signed traces, detailed timing hashes), let us know — we can deliver under an evidence packet.

If this all looks acceptable I’ll queue the credit and lock the remediation rollout schedule. We want to make sure NorthStar is comfortable with the plan before the production canary.

Apologies again for the impact, and thanks for the partnership.
